title: The oncology care system as a barrier to access: The perspectives of migrant patients and healthcare providers (MIGRA-CARE)
summary:
This study examines access barriers and unmet needs experienced by oncology patients with migrant background in Germany in (psycho-)oncological and palliative care. 

To this end, scientific articles on this topic will first be systematically evaluated. 

Subsequently, focus groups will be held with patients with migration background, relatives of patients with migration background, and healthcare professionals (e.g., oncologists, oncology nurses, psycho-oncologists, ...).

Based on this, questionnaires will be developed and used at two large cancer centers in Germany (West German Tumor Center Essen and Erlangen-EMN). The survey will include 450 oncology patients with and without migration background, at least 100 relatives with migration background, and 300 healthcare professionals involved in cancer care. The surveys will be offered in several languages (including Polish, Turkish, Russian, Italian, Arabic, Ukrainian, English, French, and German). In addition, the structures of the clinics will be examined in terms of their intercultural openness (clinic directors).

The results should show which factors at the patient level, among healthcare providers, and in institutions facilitate or hinder access to care and which unmet needs exist. This will be used to develop a model that brings together the most important influencing factors. This model will form the basis for recommendations to improve (psycho-)oncological, palliative care, and pediatric oncology care, as well as for training programs on intercultural competence for professionals.

Objectives of the study:
- Better understanding of the barriers to care and unmet needs in care for oncology patients with migration background
- Involvement of patients, relatives, and healthcare professionals
- Development of concrete recommendations for action for clinics, professionals, and the healthcare system

interventions.name:
Patients' level:
- Focus group: 8 to 10 oncology patients with migration background (classified according to the microcensus, 2022; meaning persons who themselves or at least one parent do not have German citizenship by birth)
- Survey study: 450 oncology patients with migration background

Patients' level:
- Survey study: 450 oncology patients without migration background

Patients' level:
- Focus group: 8 to 10 relatives of oncology patients with migration background (classified according to the microcensus, 2022; meaning persons who themselves or at least one parent do not have German citizenship by birth)
- Survey study: At least 100 relatives of oncology cancer

Healthcare professionals' level:
- Focus group: 8 to 10 healthcare professionals working in oncological care
- Survey study: At least 300 healthcare professionals working in oncological care

Institutional level:
- Survey study: Clinic directors of tumor centers

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients' level:
- Patients with a histologically verified oncological disease (regardless of cancer entity or stage)
- Ongoing therapy for adjuvant or palliative purposes
- Adult relatives of oncology patients
- Study consent

Professionals' level:
- Adult oncology professionals
- Study consent
Exclusion criteria:
Patients' level:
- Patients without any histologically verified oncological disease

Professionals' level:
- Not working in oncological or palliative care
